blocks.text: The Admin Sign-On Policy page displays all the sign-on rules configured for the users. The sign-on rules determine whether to allow or deny a user from accessing the Zscaler service. You can use different attributes to configure rules and apply them to the users.
The sign-on policy is not applicable to:

blocks.item: The super admin (admin@<vanityurl>.zslogin.net), as they are the primary user account that was created when onboarding your tenant.
API requests that are initiated via the OneAPI platform or legacy API workflows.

blocks.text: Sign-on policies provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Configure policies to control which users within your organization can access the Zscaler Admin Console.
Enforce condition-based access control for the users, such as trusted IP location, trusted IP location groups, etc.

blocks.heading: About the Admin Sign-On Policy Page

blocks.text: On the Admin Sign-On Policy page (Administration > Authentication > Admin Sign-On Policy), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View a list of all configured sign-on rules. For each rule, you can see:
Rule Order: The policy rule's order number. Sign-on rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order.
Rule Name: The name of the rule.
Criteria: The criteria that triggers the rule.
Rule Action: The action (Allow or Deny) taken when a rule is triggered.
Authentication Service follows the Allow rule by default, so unless a Deny rule is created, it implicitly allows everything.
Rule Status: The status (Enabled or Disabled) of the rule.
Description: The description of the rule, if available.
Enable or disable a sign-on rule.
